subject.title: [Bug]: Feishu streaming card full-content updates cause severe latency regression on long replies

question: Should Feishu expose an explicit append/delta streaming-card mode for affected tenants, or should OpenClaw keep full-content CardKit updates only and use non-streaming/cadence tuning as the supported fallback?
rationale: The current default was added to prevent truncation and matches the prior CardKit full-content contract, but the latest live repro says cadence coalescing is insufficient for some deployments, so automation cannot choose the permanent compatibility policy.

options.title: Proofed opt-in append mode
options.body: Keep full-content updates as the default, but accept a narrowly documented append/delta mode only with live Feishu proof that it fixes latency without truncation in the affected setup.

options.title: Full-content only
options.body: Reject append mode as an unsupported CardKit contract split and document streaming:false or renderMode:raw as the supported workaround for slow tenants.

options.title: Cadence-only PR
options.body: Continue with the linked coalescing PR despite the latest report, accepting that it may reduce calls without solving the core long-reply tail latency.

recommendation.title: Proofed opt-in append mode
recommendation.body: Keep full-content updates as the default, but accept a narrowly documented append/delta mode only with live Feishu proof that it fixes latency without truncation in the affected setup.

likelyOwner.reason: The package metadata names this handle as the Feishu plugin maintainer, and the decision is specific to Feishu/Lark channel behavior.
